correctness.rationale: Beta integration against b_{n,j} on a monomial of degree k≤n produces a polynomial in j with leading coefficient (n+1)!/(n+k+1)! after multiplying by n+1. The binomial expectation contributes leading coefficient n!/(n−k)!, and selfadjointness then diagonalizes M_n in shifted orthonormal Legendre polynomials. Modes above n are orthogonal to the polynomial image and vanish. The shifted recurrence has off-diagonal β_k=(k+1)/(2√((2k+1)(2k+3))); the commutator has opposite entries of absolute size β_k(λ_{n,k}−λ_{n,k+1}), including the final edge to degree n+1. Phase conjugation gives the symmetric Jacobi matrix for i√n C_n with weights a_{n,k}. Expanding the λ product for k≤R√n gives log λ=−k(k+1)/n+O_R(n^−1/2). For arbitrary k≤n, each log factor is at most −(j+1)/(n+1), since the ratio is 1−(2j+2)/(n+j+2); thus the stated Gaussian envelope holds and controls the normalized weighted ℓ^p tail for every fixed p>0. Split the compact window into blocks of length ⌊n^(1/4)⌋: the weight-deletion error has o(√n) bounded singular values, and freezing the weights within blocks gives an o(1)-norm error of rank O(√n). More generally the p-tail error is bounded by summing the p-th powers of the edge weights for the two weighted shifts, using the Schatten triangle inequality for p≥1 and trace-power subadditivity in both directions for 0<p<1. These bounds justify both perturbation and removal of the cutoff. Constant-block eigenvalues give the asserted angle-frequency integral, whose factors are the displayed gamma integrals. Substitution gives trace constant 1/π and squared Hilbert–Schmidt constant √π/(16√2). The limsup operator norm is at most twice the limiting maximum edge; a growing principal block of length o(√n) near √(n/2) attains the asymptotic value 1/√(2e). Dividing by its square gives the stable-rank constant. This applies to the classical unweighted interval operator and each fixed p, without uniformity in p or a claim about individual singular values. The supplied exact/finite spectral checker was inspected, not executed.

originality.rationale: The compact-window arcsine spectral-distribution step is already supplied by a stronger varying-recurrence theorem and is not itself novel. The supported distinct contribution is the full commutator result: exact Legendre-gap reduction and its square-root-frequency profile, integrable tail control at a scale much smaller than the full matrix size, the evaluated all-p constants, and the sharp norm edge. The known compact-window theorem alone neither controls the removed singular-value mass nor bounds the maximum. Nearby exact Durrmeyer records have different spectral observables, and no inspected theorem was found to cover the full law as a special case.
residual_risks: An unlocated semiclassical trace-ideal result incorporating the required window, tail and edge could imply more of the full claim. The stated broader Jacobi theorem has been credited for the part it does cover.

value.rationale: For a canonical finite-rank smoother and the natural position observable, the result quantifies a sharp failure of trace-class commutation despite operator-norm commutation. The nonzero trace-norm constant, diverging stable rank and entire fixed-p power scale distinguish a population of order √n weak spectral modes from an estimate of just the largest one. The finite degree is inherent to the operator, and the square-root window and critical p=1 are derived rather than arbitrary slices. The exact commutator constants are the value, not a new general Jacobi distribution method.
